headline: Dhaka ranks 10th among world’s most polluted cities
summary: The capital city continues to struggle with severe air quality issues, placing it among the top 10 most polluted urban centers globally.
details: Dhaka has been ranked as the 10th most polluted city in the world. This ranking highlights the persistent and severe air quality crisis facing the capital.
The city's air pollution is driven by various factors, including industrial emissions, vehicle exhaust, and construction dust.
Residents continue to face significant health risks due to the high levels of particulate matter in the air.
The ranking serves as a reminder of the urgent need for more effective pollution control measures and sustainable urban planning to protect public health.
caption:

headline_marked: Tribunal [[clears way for Abu Sayed murder cases]] at Rangpur court
headline: Tribunal clears way for Abu Sayed murder cases at Rangpur court
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has withdrawn its stay on two cases, allowing proceedings to resume at the Rangpur CMM court following its final verdict.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has withdrawn its stay on two murder cases involving the death of Abu Sayed, allowing proceedings to resume at the Rangpur Chief Metropolitan Magistrate (CMM) court.
The tribunal had previously stayed the cases on November 16, 2025, to avoid parallel proceedings and conflicting judgements while its own trial was underway.
The CMM court is now directed to proceed with the cases according to the law, while taking into account the tribunal's legally sound observations from its final verdict.
Abu Sayed, a student of Begum Rokeya University, was shot dead by police on July 16, 2024, during a march for quota reform, creating one of the defining images of the July Uprising.
In a separate trial, Tribunal-2 convicted 30 suspects on April 9, and sentenced two officers—Assistant Sub-Inspector Amir Hossain and Constable Sujan Chandra Roy—to death.
Other sentences included life imprisonment for three suspects and various terms ranging from 3 to 10 years for others, including former university and police officials.
Of the 30 convicted, only six are currently in custody, while 24 remain at large.
The trial involved 25 witnesses and evidence including CCTV footage and live broadcast video from NTV.
caption:
Two murder cases against the killers of Abu Sayed can now proceed in Rangpur court after the International Crimes Tribunal lifted its stay.

The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has withdrawn its stay on two murder cases involving the death of Abu Sayed, allowing proceedings to resume at the Rangpur Chief Metropolitan Magistrate (CMM) court.

The tribunal had previously stayed the cases on November 16, 2025, to avoid parallel proceedings and conflicting judgements while its own trial was underway.

The CMM court is now directed to proceed with the cases according to the law, while taking into account the tribunal's legally sound observations from its final verdict.

Abu Sayed, a student of Begum Rokeya University, was shot dead by police on July 16, 2024, during a march for quota reform, creating one of the defining images of the July Uprising.

In a separate trial, Tribunal-2 convicted 30 suspects on April 9, and sentenced two officers—Assistant Sub-Inspector Amir Hossain and Constable Sujan Chandra Roy—to death.

Other sentences included life imprisonment for three suspects and various terms ranging from 3 to 10 years for others, including former university and police officials.

Of the 30 convicted, only six are currently in custody, while 24 remain at large.

The trial involved 25 witnesses and evidence including CCTV footage and live broadcast video from NTV.

#AbuSayed #Rangpur #Justice #Bangladesh #JulyUprising

Source: Somoy News, bdnews24.com
